claims.quote: the much more practicable thing is that upper footpath, with these moving platforms beside it, running out over the street after the manner of the viaduct of an elevated railroad.
claims.description: Moving platforms will run along elevated pedestrian footpaths above the city streets.

claims.quote: But in some cases, at any rate, the demonstrated cheapness and practicability of tunnels at a considerable depth will come into play.
claims.description: Urban traffic will be carried in tunnels built at considerable depth beneath the city.

claims.quote: there is no reason but the existing filth why the roadways should not have translucent *velaria* to pull over in bright sunshine and wet weather.
claims.description: Street roadways will be covered by translucent retractable awnings that shelter traffic from sun and rain.

claims.quote: an easily portable substance, which could be decomposed electrically by wind or water power, and which would then recombine and supply force, either in intermittent thrusts at a piston, or as an electric current
claims.description: A portable substance will store energy that can be released on demand as mechanical thrust or electric current, like a rechargeable battery or fuel.

claims.quote: Their advent will be the beginning of the end for steam traction on land and of the steam ship at sea: the end indeed of the Age of Coal and Steam.
claims.description: Portable energy storage will replace steam power for land and sea transport, ending the age of coal and steam.

claims.quote: There can be little doubt that the sea speeds of 50 and even 60 miles an hour will be attained within the next few years.
claims.description: Ships will routinely reach fifty to sixty miles per hour at sea.

claims.quote: the London citizen of the year 2000 a.d. may have a choice of nearly all England and Wales south of Nottingham and east of Exeter as his suburb
claims.description: Fast transport will let a London commuter live across most of southern England and Wales.

claims.quote: the happy suggestion (for the ferry transits, at any rate) of a rail along the sea bottom, which would serve as a guide to swift submarine vessels
claims.description: A rail laid along the sea floor will guide fast submarine ferries, keeping them clear of surface motion and collisions.

claims.quote: But I do not think it at all probable that aeronautics will ever come into play as a serious modification of transport and communication
claims.description: Aircraft will never become a serious means of transport or communication.

claims.quote: There is hardly any reason, beyond this tradition of the horse, why the railway carriage should not be even nine or ten feet wide
claims.description: Railway carriages could be made nine or ten feet wide with far more room and smoother ride than current carriages.

claims.quote: It is much more probable that these coming cities will not be, in the old sense, cities at all; they will present a new and entirely different phase of human distribution.
claims.description: Future great cities will be dispersed over wide areas rather than dense, so they will no longer resemble the cities of the past.
